declarations.name: baseVersion
declarations.description:
The version of `@unicorne/components`. A registration carries it: two
copies of the base on a page can tell their versions apart (ADR 0012).

Base class every component extends.

Kept intentionally thin: universal resets/properties and the registration
contract only. Behavior that not every component needs (open/close, focus
delegation, form association, ...) belongs in a mixin from `src/mixins`.
Custom events are dispatched as typed `Event` subclasses from
`src/events`, not through a generic base-class `emit()` helper — see
`src/events/modal-close.ts` for the pattern.

Classes never register themselves (ADR 0001, D1): `defineComponents()`
registers a subclass per prefix (`u-button`, `acme-button`, ...) and
hands it the tag names of its registration through `tagNames`.
declarations.name: DSBaseElement

declarations.description:
Reactive controller: shows a popover of the host's shadow root in the top
layer, below an element of the same shadow root, its anchor: the list of an
autocomplete, a menu, a tooltip (ADR 0009, D2).

Each `[popover]` of the shadow root is a `popover="manual"`: the component
decides when it closes (Escape, a click outside, a choice). The controller
sets `data-open` on it while it's open: the CSS writes its open state on
`[data-open]`, not on `:popover-open`, which the oldest browsers of the
matrix lack. With an exit transition, the open state is
`[data-open]:where(:not([data-closing]))`.

The popover sits below its anchor, aligned with its start edge, at least
as wide, and flips when it would overflow the viewport. Its block margin
is the space between them. Where CSS anchor positioning is missing, the
controller loads Floating UI and positions it from script: the popover also
shrinks to the space left, down to its `max-block-size`. Without the
Popover API, there is no top layer: the popover is fixed above the page
(`--u-z-index-overlay`), and an ancestor that clips its overflow clips it.

Out of the document, a popover leaves the top layer: the controller closes
those it opened when the host disconnects.
declarations.name: AnchoredPopoverController

declarations.description:
Reactive controller: lets a component take commands from invoker buttons
(Invoker Commands, ADR 0008): a native `<button commandfor="id"
command="--name">`, or a component with `withInvoker` (`button`).

The browser runs a built-in command (`show-modal`) only on a native
`<dialog>` or popover, and never sends it to a custom element. A component
takes custom commands, prefixed with `--`.

`handle` runs a command sent to the component: `event.command` is its
name, `event.source` the button, retargeted to its host. Handle the
component's `--` commands and ignore the others: the polyfill also sends
built-in ones.

Where Invoker Commands are missing, the first connected component loads
invokers-polyfill: the page's native invoker buttons need it too.

Reactive controller: a list of options in the host's shadow root,
`role="listbox"`, whose active option follows the keyboard while the focus
stays on a control: the input of an autocomplete, the button of a select
(ADR 0009). The control takes `activeDescendant` as its
`aria-activedescendant`, and `id` as its `aria-controls`.

The controller connects a list to the DOM; it holds no state of its own.
The host owns the active index (`comboboxReducer()`, or
`moveActiveIndex()` of `state/listbox.ts`) and the options.

It also reads the `<option>` children of the host, as data, in
`childOptions`, and never changes them: a framework keeps rendering them.
Either way, the list renders its own copies, in the shadow root of the
control: `aria-activedescendant` only reaches an element of its own tree
(ADR 0007). `render()` also renders the hidden slot of these children.

On a server, the host has no children to read: a host rendered there
(ADR 0014) reads them after its first render, which then matches the
server's.

An alert component that displays a message to the user.

The icon of its type comes first: the icon of the same name, from the

declarations.description:
A text field with suggestions: the list below the input shows the
suggestions that match the text, and the user picks one or keeps typing.
The value is the text, free: a suggestion only fills it, as `<input list>`
does. The label, the hint, the error and the form behavior are those of
`FieldBase`; the popup and its state are those of `ComboboxBase`; the list
is that of a `ListboxController`.

The suggestions are `options`, or else the `<option>` children of the
field. With `filter="none"`, the application filters them itself: it
listens to `input` and sets `options`, from a server for instance. New
options open the list while the user types.

Keys, list open: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move to the next and previous
suggestion, looping at the ends; Enter picks the active one; Escape closes
the list and keeps the text; Home, End and the other keys edit the text.
Enter without an active suggestion closes the list.

While the user types, a live region announces the number of suggestions:
`resultsMessage` writes it.

The browser's own suggestions (`autocomplete`) are off by default: they
would cover the list. Give `autocomplete` to have both.

declarations.description:
Shared base of the comboboxes: a form field whose control opens a popup
below it, `autocomplete` for instance. Abstract: extend `Autocomplete`, or
write a combobox with `renderCombobox()` and `renderPopup()`. The label,
the hint, the error and the form behavior are those of `FieldBase`.

Its state is that of `comboboxReducer()` (`state/combobox.ts`, ADR 0010):
whether the popup is open, which of its items is active, whether it follows
what the user types. The base sends it the events of the control, and
shows the popup it describes.

The control keeps the focus while the popup is open, and names the
popup's content with `aria-controls`: both are in the same shadow root
(ADR 0009). The popup is a `popover="manual"` in the top layer, anchored
by an `AnchoredPopoverController`, with an animated entry and exit.

Keys of the control, popup closed: ArrowDown and ArrowUp open it and enter
it at its first or last item, Alt+ArrowDown opens it without entering.
Popup open: Escape and Alt+ArrowUp close it, Tab closes it and moves on;
the others go to `handlePopupKeydown()`. The popup also closes when the
focus leaves the field, when the field is disabled, and when its form is
reset. Escape closes only the popup, not a modal around the field.

A polite live region announces `popupStatus`, the number of suggestions
for instance: the popup's content changes without the focus moving.

label stays in the shadow root of its control: an `id` doesn't cross a

and left the field, or once validation has run (a submission attempt,
`checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`), then follows each keystroke. The
message is the browser's, in the browser's language: give `error-message`

members.name: renderControl
members.description:
Renders the native control, between the hint and the error message. It
has `id="control"` (the label's `for`), `class="control"` (the styles)
and its own part. It binds `.value=${live(this.value)}`, `required`,
`disabled` (`isDisabled`), `autocomplete`, its constraints,
`controlInvalid`, `controlDescribedBy`, `handleInput` and
`handleChange`. A single-line control also binds
`@keydown=${this.submitOnEnter}`.

members.name: customStates
members.default: { set: (name: string, active: boolean) => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return; } if (active) { this.internals.states.add(name); } else { this.internals.states.delete(name); } }, has: (name: string): boolean => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return false; } return this.internals.states.has(name); }, }
members.description:
Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.
A no-op where `:state()` is unsupported (see `supportsCustomStates`), so
`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

members.name: submitOnEnter
members.description:
For the `keydown` listener of a single-line control: Enter submits the
form, as HTML's implicit submission does for a native `<input>`. With a
submit button in the form, the form is submitted unless the first one
is disabled. Without any, it is submitted when this field is its only
single-line one. Does nothing for a key another listener has handled,
nor while an input method composes the text.

The tag of a component declared in `static dependencies`, for templates
from `lit/static-html.js`: `` html`<${this.tagFor(Button)}>…</${…}>` ``.

`u-button`, `acme-modal` renders `acme-button` — the brand's override
